title: Spine inclination and hip range of forward flexion, young vs elderly (skin markers)
condition: healthy, standing, upright to end of forward flexion

quantity.name: range of flexion
quantity.definition: spine inclination = C7-sacrum vector vs vertical; hip = pelvis vs upper leg; at end of flexion relative to upright

source.authors: Ignasiak D, Rüeger A, Ferguson SJ
source.n: 42 subjects (21 young: 13 F/8 M; 21 elderly: 13 F/8 M)
source.sample: healthy volunteers without spinal surgery, chronic spine disorder or recent back pain; 44 recruited, 42 analysed

protocol.summary: No significant age difference in inclination or hip ROF; elderly hips median ~84 vs ~78 deg.
how_to_use: Use median (IQR) end-of-flexion ROF for young vs elderly; elderly use ~11 deg less lumbar flexion and more hip flexion for a similar spine inclination.
Region definitions are skin-curve based: thoracic C7-L1, lumbar L1-sacrum, hip = pelvis vs upper leg; spine inclination = C7-sacrum vector vs vertical.

measurement.device: Vicon MX 12 cameras, 100 Hz; 11 spinous-process markers (C7,T3,T5,T7,T9,T11,L1-L5) + sacrum; cubic polynomial fitted to marker curve, segment angles from curve normals
measurement.posture: standing, feet hip-width, knees extended, arms relaxed
measurement.task: slow forward flexion at self-selected speed to end of range and return

extraction.uncertainty: ±1.5 deg (low-resolution raster figure, 2.66 px/deg at 400 dpi)
extraction.check_notes: Box edges/medians from colour run profiles; elderly hip median read in an unclassified-colour gap between fills (±2 deg).

pass_rule.rule: input data – not graded; use for robustness checks
